acceptance: A finding is treated as pre-existing only with verified evidence that the defective behaviour exists at the base commit and the change does not create or worsen it; unverifiable claims block.
Proven pre-existing non-Critical findings are recorded as known defects in a durable, queryable place for follow-up, and are visible on the PR; they do not block the gate.
Critical findings always block, pre-existing or not.
Tests prove a disguised new defect (unchanged span, changed behaviour) still blocks, a genuine base defect is logged and not blocking, and a Critical base defect blocks.
Shipped in a Theseus release and adopted by BenchBox.
context: Sequencing: #54's fail-closed D4 ships in the current combined release (safe: every finding blocks). BenchBox adoption omits pre_existing: advisory until this lands.
description: Owner rule 2026-11-09: the reviewer must be able to identify that a defect was pre-existing and not created by the current change. Such findings are logged as known defects for later follow-up and do not block the PR, UNLESS the defect is Critical, which still blocks. Theseus #45 added advisory demotion, but the #4062 review (D4) found it accepted unchanged line spans without proving the behaviour existed at the base, and #54 removes demotion entirely (every finding blocks). This item designs and ships a provable mechanism.
